title: Billing Efficiency adds up all hours first, not an average of advisors
custom_preconds:
1. Sign in on the build under test as an Admin user. Admin holds every permission, including Reports, so Reports and Dashboard both show in the top menu.
  2. In the top bar, click the location name at the top left (e.g. ShopHub) and choose your test location: one where nobody else invoices, issues credits or clocks time this week. The next step checks that it is quiet. If no location you can reach is quiet, create one once and reuse it on every later run: Settings > Locations > add a location (e.g. "ZZAUTOTEST Dashboard Quiet") > save, give your user access, then choose it here. Locations cannot be deleted, so never create a second one.
  3. Check the location is quiet: click Dashboard in the top menu, click the range pill on the Billing Efficiency tile and choose This Week. It must show no percentage (a grey "-", or "n/a" on an older build). If it shows a percentage, choose another location.
  4. Run the whole case on one day, and not on the last evening of the week, so every record you create stays inside This Week.
  5. Create a test customer: Customers > New Customer, name it (e.g. "ZZAUTOTEST Dash Customer 1") and save. On its Contacts tab add a contact (e.g. "Dana Test"). On its Assets tab add an asset (e.g. unit "ZZ-101") and pick that contact in the asset's Contact field.
  6. Have a technician who works at this location and can clock time (e.g. "Tom Tech"): Settings > Staff > open the technician and check the Time Clock setting is on. You need this technician's sign-in to clock time in a second browser or a private window.
  7. Have two staff members in the work order's Service Advisor list (e.g. "Alex Advisor" and "Bea Advisor").
  8. Work order A (low efficiency, many hours). Create and invoice it with these standard steps:
    • Work Orders > New Work Order > choose the customer and its asset > Create.
    • In the work order header set Service Advisor to "Alex Advisor" and enter the mileage (e.g. 123456). If the Finance tab is greyed out with "Please select a contact for the asset", choose the contact and answer YES to keep it on the asset.
    • Lines tab > New Line: Description "ZZAUTOTEST A", Technician "Tom Tech", Labor Rate e.g. $100.00 per hour, Estimated Time 1.00, Tech Time 1.00, tick Approved > Save & Close.
    • In the second browser, signed in as Tom Tech: Work Orders > open this work order > use Clock In on the line, then clock out.
    • Make the clocked time exact: on the work order click the three dots (top right) > Timesheets (1) and edit the record so it runs exactly 4.00 hours earlier today (e.g. 7:00 AM to 11:00 AM). If the time cannot be edited there or in Reports > Timesheet Activities, keep the real time and use the hours Timesheet Activities shows instead of 4.00 in every sum below.
    • On each line type a Story (e.g. "Done") and set the line to Complete. Then click Complete Work Order, then Mark Reviewed.
    • Finance tab > Create Invoice. When the New Customer Payment dialog opens, close it without taking a payment. Do not send or pay the invoice.
  9. Work order B (high efficiency, few hours). Create and invoice it the same way:
    • Work Orders > New Work Order > choose the customer and its asset > Create.
    • In the work order header set Service Advisor to "Bea Advisor" and enter the mileage (e.g. 123456). If the Finance tab is greyed out with "Please select a contact for the asset", choose the contact and answer YES to keep it on the asset.
    • Lines tab > New Line: Description "ZZAUTOTEST B", Technician "Tom Tech", Labor Rate e.g. $100.00 per hour, Estimated Time 2.00, Tech Time 2.00, tick Approved > Save & Close.
    • In the second browser, signed in as Tom Tech: Work Orders > open this work order > use Clock In on the line, then clock out.
    • Make the clocked time exact: on the work order click the three dots (top right) > Timesheets (1) and edit the record so it runs exactly 1.00 hours earlier today (e.g. 11:00 AM to 12:00 PM). If the time cannot be edited there or in Reports > Timesheet Activities, keep the real time and use the hours Timesheet Activities shows instead of 1.00 in every sum below.
    • On each line type a Story (e.g. "Done") and set the line to Complete. Then click Complete Work Order, then Mark Reviewed.
    • Finance tab > Create Invoice. When the New Customer Payment dialog opens, close it without taking a payment. Do not send or pay the invoice.
custom_steps:
1. Work out the right figure by hand, all hours first: (1.00 + 2.00) / (4.00 + 1.00) x 100 = 3.00 / 5.00 x 100 = 60.00%.
  2. Work out the wrong figure, an average of the two advisors: Alex 1.00 / 4.00 = 25.00%, Bea 2.00 / 1.00 = 200.00%, average (25.00 + 200.00) / 2 = 112.50%.
  3. Click Dashboard in the top menu.
  4. On the Billing Efficiency tile click the range pill and choose This Week.
  5. Write down the percentage and the line under it.
  6. Click the arrow icon beside "Billing Efficiency" on the tile (its tooltip names the report).
  7. On Service Advisor Analysis set the Date control to This week with no advisor chosen.
  8. Write down each invoice row's Billing Efficiency and the Totals row Billing Efficiency.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • The tile reads 60.00% (3.00 / 5.00 x 100), not 112.50%.
  • The line under it reads "3.00 Invoiced / 5.00 Clocked".
  • The report shows Alex's invoice at 25.00% and Bea's at 200.00%, and its Totals row reads 60.00%, the same as the tile.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-490; story SV-9575 (S3); Dashboard v1 PRD, Confluence 788430850 v42, read 7 Oct 2026, S3 (S3-R2 Billing Efficiency row, S3-R1, context note). Design canvas (claude.ai/artifact/Wae9DFQ8PJQBy8mbLsL5ge, captured 2026-09-28) used for on-screen labels and navigation only: boards 05_Billing_After, 11_service-advisor-analysis_After.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S3-R2: “Each measure is calculated as defined in the table below.”
  • S3-R2 table row (Billing Efficiency): “| Billing Efficiency | Invoiced hours divided by worked hours, times 100, for the selected range. | Service Advisor Analysis report |”
  • S3-R1: “Every figure the dashboard shows for a measure equals the figure the measure's matching report shows for the same workplace, date range, and filters. This holds at every moment, not merely in principle. The dashboard may serve a figure from a cache, but only in a way that cannot produce a difference: the tile and its report must resolve to the same stored calculation, or the cache must be invalidated by the same events that change the report's answer. A tile that shows a different number from its report because one of them is more recently computed than the other is a defect, not an accepted staleness window. There is no freshness allowance and no "up to N minutes behind" in this spec.”
  • S3 context note (parity check): “to check parity on a KPI tile that shows a shop-wide figure, compare it against the matching report with all advisors or all technicians selected (no filter applied).”

Last checked against build v26.39.1-09be696 on 10/2/2026.
